expectations.text: Rejects the 50-partner target as unachievable from zero supply in 10 weeks and says so plainly rather than hedging
expectations.evidence: The bottom line opens with: "'At least 50 partners on stage' cannot be met honestly in 10 weeks. Nessforth has no apps, no reviewer and no pipeline." It adds that "10 weeks supports single digits, not 50" and gives a dedicated 'Why 50 fails' section. The rejection is stated plainly and up front, and it names the zero-supply cause. The alternative options (logos slide, slipping the launch) are offered with the 50 explicitly reframed as a roadmap and never as launch partners, so they don't weaken the rejection.

expectations.text: Rejects the 50-partner target as unachievable from zero supply in 10 weeks and says so plainly rather than hedging
expectations.evidence: The first line, in bold, says: "'50 partners on stage' can't be 50 shipped, reviewed apps. Reset the number this week." It grounds this in the zero starting point ("You have zero apps, no reviewer and no pipeline"), in third-party build time (4–6 weeks) and in partner attrition, then gives a concrete lower target: 10–15 live apps and 25–35 logos in total. It says a 50-logo wall is possible only if unshipped partners are labeled "Coming soon", and adds "Don't present them as live apps." That is a reframe, not a hedge.
